record.title: CausalWAM adds sparse action-relevance routing to a world-action model
record.summary: The CausalWAM preprint presents an identifiability result for action-relevant latent factors under support-sparsity assumptions and reports adding a sparse router to a world-action model. In author-run evaluations, the paper reports gains over its baseline on 13 of 17 RoboCasa365 tasks (macro success 0.24 to 0.43), higher results across 40 LIBERO tasks, and a majority of successes over the baseline in 50 Franka cube-stack trials per policy. These are single-preprint results, not independent replications. The implementation retains a dense visual-to-action path; the paper's routed-only intervention covers four selected high-success tasks and does not establish that the learned theoretical support alone drives actions generally.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Under the paper's support-sparsity and regularity assumptions, its theorem states that the action-relevant latent block can be identified up to permutation and invertible transformation, separating it from nuisance factors.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors' RoboCasa365 evaluation, CausalWAM reports macro success increasing from 0.24 to 0.43 over the baseline, with improvement on 13 of 17 tasks and 100 episodes per task.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report higher results across 40 LIBERO tasks and majority success over the baseline in 50 Franka real-robot cube-stack trials per policy; the inspected paper does not provide independent replication of these outcomes.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish that the mathematical support identified by its theorem is the sole or necessary information path driving deployed actions: its implementation retains a dense visual-to-action pathway, and its routed-only C-only intervention is reported only on four selected high-success tasks.

evidence_gaps.description: The simulation and real-robot results have not been independently reproduced.
Transfer beyond the reported Cosmos 3 Nano, RoboCasa365, LIBERO and cube-stack conditions is not established.
The contribution of sparse routed factors versus the retained dense visual-to-action pathway is unresolved outside four selected C-only intervention tasks.

brief.importance_rationale: A potentially meaningful method for robot world-action models, backed by explicit theory and author-reported results across simulation suites and a small real-robot experiment. Importance is moderate because it could improve causal/action-relevant representations if true, while the evidence is a single preprint, the implementation retains a dense action path, and transfer and independent replication are unestablished.
limitations: Results are reported in one preprint and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The theoretical identifiability result depends on support-sparsity and regularity assumptions; the paper notes that individual latents are not component-wise identifiable.

The deployed architecture includes a dense visual-to-action path alongside sparse routing, so the implementation does not by itself demonstrate that actions depend only on the theorem's selected support.
The routed-only C-only ablation covers four selected top-success tasks; it does not establish sufficiency across the reported task suites.
Generality beyond the tested model, tasks, data and hardware remains unknown.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that a sparse router improves macro RoboCasa365 task success from 0.24 to 0.43, with gains on 13 of 17 tasks; they also report higher results across 40 LIBERO tasks and majority success over baseline in 50 Franka cube-stack trials per policy.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint describes the method and reports these measurements. This activation did not independently reproduce them; they remain author-reported claims.
technical.mechanism: The paper seeks latent factors that support actions while excluding nuisance factors, proves identifiability under support-sparsity and regularity assumptions, and adds a learned sparse router and sparsity loss to the action head of a world-action model.
technical.regime: One preprint's implementation based on Cosmos 3 Nano. Reported evaluations include RoboCasa365 (17 tasks, 100 episodes per task), LIBERO (40 tasks), and Franka real-robot cube stacking (50 trials per policy). The C-only routed-path intervention is reported on four selected top-success tasks.
technical.reproducibility: Full arXiv HTML including theory, experiments and appendices was inspected. No independent reproduction or public code repository was established in this bounded check.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares its model with its stated baseline under the same reported evaluation suites and reports per-task RoboCasa365 outcomes; the present record treats those comparisons as author claims, not independent confirmation.

brief.title: CausalWAM adds sparse action-relevance routing to a world-action model
brief.why_it_matters: If independently reproduced and transferable, identifying and routing action-relevant visual factors could improve data efficiency and robustness in learned robot policies. The present evidence is promising but bounded to author-run experiments and one model family; the gap between the support-sparsity theorem and the deployed architecture is material.
